items.title: Crude oil pulls back.
items.excerpt: Bob Iaccino covers the morning's market action, noting that U.S. equities are mixed while Russell 2000 futures lead. He discusses shifting rate hike expectations, with the probability of a December move rising to 75.5% while long-end Treasury yields fall. Iaccino also recaps global economic data, including unchanged Chinese interest rates and worse-than-expected European sentiment readings, before looking ahead to heavy earnings and upcoming U.K. CPI and EIA crude inventory data.

items.excerpt: Roche reports its nine-month sales on 22 October 2026, after a rise of about 9% since July. One investor wants to buy lower, another already owns the shares. How can each name a price and be paid to wait? Before a company reports, options on its shares tend to cost more than in a quiet week. Whoever sells the option collects that extra. Roche publishes its nine-month sales on Thursday 22 October 2026 at 07:00 CET, before the Swiss market opens. The shares closed at CHF 380.10, about 9% higher than after the July results (Source: Saxo price data, as of 19 October 2026). In commodities, gold, silver and crude oil push higher, while copper and bitcoin drop. Markets look ahead to Federal Reserve speakers Kevin Warsh and Beth Hammack for any signal on inflation and interest rates before the next FOMC meeting.
